name: Kaomoji and Emoticon
summary: A face made of punctuation and letters, set in a line of plain text. It came from 1980s bulletin boards: the sideways :-) in the West and the upright (^_^) in Japan.

philosophy.core_thesis: A face needs no picture: a few characters of one text font, in one colour, carry a whole feeling.
design_principles: Build each face from 3 to 12 characters of the same monospace font, in one colour and one size.
Set the face on a plain ground of #FFFDF5 with text at #1A1A1A, with no border and no fill.
Keep the face inline with the text, on the same baseline, with 1 space before and after.
Use the upright Japanese form (^_^) for the eyes and mouth, and the sideways Western form :-) only for short chat lines.
Limit one message to 1 or 2 faces; repeat a character (^^^, !!!) up to 3 times for emphasis.
Set the body text in a 16px mono font at a line height of 1.6, and let the face take the same size.
Render the faces at an integer pixel size, with no anti-aliased scaling above 200%.
anti_patterns: Coloured emoji pictures in place of characters
Faces that need a picture font to display
Gradients, shadows and glossy fills behind the face
More than 3 faces in one line
Proportional fonts that break the face alignment
Faces drawn at a size different from the text

layout.grid_mechanics: A single column of text lines on a monospace grid; each character cell is 0.6em wide and 1.6em high.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 40% to 60% of the surface stays empty; the spacing scale is 8, 16 and 32px.
layout.alignment_rules: Flush-left lines; a face sits inside a line, never on a line of its own except as a sign-off.
layout.container_geometry: Plain text blocks with 0px radius; a 1px rule or a 1px box of the text colour marks a message.

font_pairings.note: A Japanese dot-matrix face for the display line, with a clean mono text face.
A terminal face for pure Western emoticon pages.

typography.tracking: Display 0.05em; body 0em, with fixed character width.
hierarchy_rules: Use one size for the whole page: 16px body and 24px for the single display line.
Mark a heading with a line of === or --- characters, not with a size jump.
Show a face at the size of the text around it.
Keep the page to one colour of ink, and show emphasis with a repeated character.

color.palette_structure: Near-black ink on warm paper, with one pink for a single highlighted face.
color.contrast_rules: Ink on paper reaches 16:1; the blush accent marks one face and does not carry body text.
color.surface_treatment: Flat paper with no gradient; an optional 1px rule between lines.
color.light_and_shadow: No light and no shadow; the surface is flat like a terminal line.

materiality.surface_simulation: Plain terminal text on paper: no material, only glyphs.
materiality.border_rules: A 1px line in the ink colour, or none.

ornamentation_details.illustration: ASCII line art of up to 12 lines in the same mono font.

motion.transition_physics: Text appears at once or types in at 40ms for each character; faces do not move.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover underlines a link with a 1px line; active inverts ink and paper.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels a small, friendly human tone in a plain text line.

use_cases: friendly empty states in a CLI
avoid_when: The brand needs a formal tone.
The page needs full colour emoji for a wide audience.
The text font lacks the characters of the face.

modifiers.how: Replace each face with a colour emoji glyph of the same size and keep the text line.
Set the page on black with a green mono face and add ANSI colour blocks.
Swap the face for a looped clip of 2 to 4 seconds with a caption line.

pack.why: A pixel family fits faces built on a character grid, with square terminals.

ground.why: A kaomoji lives on the plain paper of a text line, so the ground stays flat.
